summary:
## Idea
Game.Core Los provides Bresenham and supercover traces and endpoint line-of-sight checks. The exact grade applies specifically to LineMode and lineOfSightBy.

## Complexity
Line/LOS work scales with the grid line length and transparency callback cost; producing a trace stores its visited cells.

## Use when
Grid visibility queries should share Game.Core cell and occlusion conventions.

## Avoid when
Continuous visibility polygons are needed, or another trace variant is assumed exact without profile evidence.

## Pitfalls
Select LineMode deliberately at corner crossings. Only Los.lineOfSightBy is explicitly LockstepExact; line, supercover, trace and lineOfSight remain Unclassified in the cited profile. Deterministic transparency is required.

## F# usage
Package: FS.GG.Game.Core; cited source API (resolve your actual package pin).
`FS.GG.Game.Core.Los.lineOfSightBy: LineMode -> (Cell -> bool) -> Cell -> Cell -> bool`

```fsharp
open FS.GG.Game.Core
let canSee mode (a: Cell) (b: Cell) =
    Los.lineOfSightBy mode (fun _ -> true) a b
```

## Tests
LosTests includes the exhaustive small-grid symmetry evidence referenced by ADR0098, plus line/trace cases. Profile fixture operation3 covers lineOfSightBy, not every helper.

## Bench
Owed: technique-specific timing baseline under https://github.com/FS-GG/FS.GG.Game/issues/804. No timing or cross-runtime performance claim is made here.

## References
Bresenham, Algorithm for computer control of a digital plotter, IBM Systems Journal, 1965. The Game.Core contract defines supercover/corner behaviour.
